key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as markets price in a fourth RBA rate hike, with house prices forecast to fall up to 10% on record
CBA reports home loan applications down 15% since the federal budget, signalling severe credit contraction
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
Bathla's collapse exposes systemic fragility in Australia's construction and housing finance chain
ASIC launches review of whistleblower complaints at Big Four accounting firms, raising governance concerns
Small-cap miners (Kaoko Metals, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) show relative strength
Energy transition costs mounting; TMK Energy gas rates surge; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny intensifies
RBA cautioned against further hikes given weak GDP, creating policy uncertainty

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; small-cap explorers (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) outperform on capital raises and assay results; Macarthur clears WA iron ore bulk test hurdle
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin pressure from demand softness; small-caps offer speculative upside but carry elevated execution risk

sectors.trend: CBA.AX flags 15% drop in home loan applications; banks forecast record house price declines; legal loophole allowing CBA and Westpac to overcharge loyal customers draws scrutiny; ASIC reviews Big Four accountants
sectors.implications: Credit growth contraction pressures NIM; potential NPL build-out in 2027; governance risk from accounting sector review; CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX under pressure

sectors.trend: TMK Energy gas rates surge ahead of Mongolian drilling; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny; energy transition costs 'running off the rails'; natural gas demand from data centres (Musk/Munster commentary)
sectors.implications: Santos.AX, Woodside.AX, Boral.AX benefit from gas pricing; transition-cost overhang weighs on renewables names; data-centre power demand a structural tailwind

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse signals broader construction sector distress; housing construction to follow falling prices; Melbourne councils admit infrastructure cannot cope with population growth; Victoria's debt flagged by ratings agencies
sectors.implications: REITs (GP.AX, SPG.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and cap-rate risk; construction names (WTC.AX, MDS.AX) under stress; residential REITs vulnerable to 10% price correction

sectors.trend: Nvidia confirms AI boom intact; Dell posts strong quarter on AI demand; Goldman/BofA stablecoin bet; Palantir/Salesforce rebound; Australia faces AI worker shortage
sectors.implications: ASX tech (WES.AX, XRO.AX) benefits from global AI capex cycle; data-centre power demand supports energy names; skilled-migration policy (headline 9) is a structural tailwind

sectors.trend: EV sales overtake petrol cars for first time in Australia; hidden costs (charging, battery) emerging; Volkswagen cutting 50,000 jobs globally
sectors.implications: Wesfarmers.AX, Coles.GR face margin pressure from fuel-cost-driven consumer shift; auto supply-chain names under stress; EV infrastructure plays gain relevance

key_themes: RBA rate-hike uncertainty: fourth hike looming but GDP weakness creates policy paralysis
Housing correction: 10% price fall forecast, 15% loan-application drop, construction contraction
Iron ore structural shakeout masked by geopolitical noise
Construction sector fragility (Bathla) as a systemic warning
Energy transition cost overhang vs. gas/data-centre demand tailwind
Small-cap mining relative strength amid large-cap weakness
Global AI capex cycle intact; Australia's AI/tradie skills gap
Credit contraction and governance scrutiny (ASIC, Big Four)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA fourth rate hike triggering housing correction
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and construction exposure; favour fixed-income and dividend-defensive names; monitor RBA statement for forward guidance

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore demand shakeout / China slowdown
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from pure iron-ore exposure; favour gold (A2M.AX, NGT.AX) and diversified miners
Avoid leveraged construction and residential development names; monitor ASX construction index

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Credit contraction / NPL build-out at major banks
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor CBA.AX, NAB.AX loan-loss provisions; favour banks with stronger capital buffers

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy transition cost overrun / policy reversal
risk_assessment.mitigation: Favour gas-exposed names (Santos.AX, Boral.AX) over pure renewables; watch federal energy policy

risk_assessment.risk_factor: ASIC / Big Four governance scandal spillover
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor for any ASX-listed company audit-firm changes; limited direct market impact

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and diversified miners as iron ore weakens
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore shakeout pressures BHP/RIO/FMG; gold benefits from rate-hike uncertainty and safe-haven flows; Aurum and small-caps show momentum

opportunities.recommendation: Add gas-exposed energy names on data-centre power demand
opportunities.rationale: TMK gas rates surge; Musk/Munster confirm natural gas for data centres; structural demand tailwind offsets transition-cost noise

opportunities.recommendation: Selective small-cap mining exposure on capital raises
opportunities.rationale: Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals showing relative strength; high-risk/high-reward in a risk-off tape
In a rate-hike, housing-correction environment, high-yield defensives (WES.AX, WBC.AX) offer income and relative stability

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce residential REIT and construction exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: 10% house-price fall forecast, 15% loan-application drop, Bathla collapse signal sector-wide stress; construction to follow prices lower

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge rate-hike risk with short-duration bonds or inverse ASX ETFs
defensive_moves.rationale: Fourth RBA hike looming; ASX closed week lower; GDP weakness creates two-way policy risk
Structural shakeout underway; geopolitical distraction masks fundamental demand deterioration

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish-to-neutral. ASX likely to trade lower into a probable fourth RBA hike. Housing data (15% loan drop, 10% price forecast) will pressure financials and REITs. Small-cap miners and gold offer relative strength. Volatility elevated.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. 'Bull case returns' thesis supported by global AI capex cycle, energy transition demand, and eventual RBA pivot. However, housing correction and credit contraction may delay recovery into 2027. Diversified miners and gas names best positioned.
key_catalysts: Iron ore price trajectory / China stimulus signals
Housing credit data and NPL trends at major banks
Global AI capex guidance (Nvidia, Dell earnings)
watch_list: RBA cash rate and statement (September meeting)
